title: Realistic Hupsel daily atmospheric workload for S4
central_question: Does the P5-qualified S4 research implementation retain useful profile/storage behaviour and computational advantage under a real 60-day Hupsel meteorological sequence when atmospheric demand is imposed as an explicit top-boundary proxy?

prospective_classification.REALISTIC_DAILY_APPROXIMATE: candidate completes and timing error is zero, while continuous errors remain explicit
prospective_classification.REALISTIC_DAILY_TIMING_SENSITIVE: candidate completes and Reference-observable extrema timing error is nonzero
prospective_classification.REALISTIC_DAILY_NUMERICAL_BLOCKED: candidate does not complete under the frozen P5 policy

gates.equation_binding: compiled candidate and Richards reference receive byte-identical frozen daily delta series
gates.numerical: candidate ledger <=1e-8 cm and complete 60-day output for both initial states
gates.speed: same-runner candidate/R128 median process wall ratio reported; <1 supports workload-specific speed advantage
gates.no_application_threshold: No absolute hydrological acceptance threshold is introduced.

interpretation_limits: Rain and ETref are authentic daily Hupsel meteorological values from a pinned public copy.
ETref is used only as an imposed top-boundary extraction proxy. It is not actual evaporation, transpiration or root uptake.
This is therefore realistic atmospheric forcing, not a whole-Hupsel simulation or application validation.
The public copy supports workload provenance but is not substituted for the exact official Hupsel raw-file authority.
